title: Mouse movement
help: Sends a relative movement with Windows SendInput. Positive X moves right; positive Y moves down. Delay postpones the start. Duration 0 or one step sends the whole motion at once; multiple steps distribute the exact total ΔX/ΔY across the duration. For one action per key press, use If key down → On new press. For repeated motion while held, choose While held and Repeat until stopped. A second block with negative deltas can reverse the motion after a Wait. This does not measure or set a game's camera position. Stop with Ctrl+Alt+F7. Use macros only where permitted.

help: Finds the selected element and invokes, enters text, toggles, selects or reads it. Result and error text go into variables; errors take the Error output. title: Select option
help: Shows one choice per line (1–100 choices, up to 250 characters each). Press Enter between choices in the block properties. In graph code, those line breaks appear as \n within one value line; the properties show separate choices. A template \& in properties appears as \\& in code because the code also escapes the backslash. Each line may contain a template such as =[(${counter}+2)*3]& units \&: with counter=1 it displays ‘9 units &’. OK returns the chosen 1-based index; cancel or OK without a selection returns 0. Stopping closes the dialog. Set title, X/Y and size in the block. Leave both X/Y blank to center on screen. Blank dimensions grow to fit the question and choices, starting at 465×410. Explicit width is 360–3000 and height 260–3000 pixels. X/Y are screen coordinates, not graph coordinates.
note: Run once and inspect the execution journal. The featured block records its actions; surrounding blocks prepare input or show the result. The first option displays 9 units &: [] evaluates math, & joins text, and \& prints a literal &. In properties, 11 and 22 are separate lines; graph code writes the breaks as \n.
